# Supervised Stage

The supervised stage is the second methodological block of the workflow. It is a one-year probabilistic classifier that learns a burned-area score from the deterministic decisions of the same year and scenario. The operational entry point is the package function `run_oneyear_supervised_pipeline()`, which orchestrates the modular stages (pools, folds, features, OOF diagnostics, final model, scoring). Each stage is also exported as a standalone function so the workflow can be driven step by step; calling a stage directly produces byte-identical outputs to a full orchestrated run.

LOYO (leave-one-year-out) remains a separate temporal-validation concept and is not represented by an active current runtime.

## Current Status

- The supervised one-year pipeline is the current operational patch-level runtime, implemented entirely inside the package (`R/supervised-*.R` and the internal engines `R/internal-sup-*.R`). There is no `sys.source()` of external legacy scripts and no namespace mutation.
- The unburned-pool strategy is fixed: `all_sources` is the only mode and is applied implicitly in every run. The user-selectable knob was removed on 2026-06-05, and the former `deterministic_direct` baseline strategy no longer exists. A stale `negative_pool_policy` / `otsu_unburned_generation` option errors rather than being silently ignored (passing `negative_pool_policy = "all_sources"` is accepted as an informational no-op).

## Inputs And Support Layers

The supervised stage starts from the deterministic outputs of the same year and scenario.

| Input group | Current role |
|---|---|
| `internal_decisions` | Defines the polygon universe to relabel, train, score, and filter |
| Main `change_index` mosaic | Main burned-sensitive predictor surface |
| `delayed_change_index` | Optional persistence-style (autumn-winter) support layer used in feature extraction |
| DEM and slope | Topographic predictors |
| CORINE land-cover support | Polygon-level land-cover composition features |
| Hotspots when available | Optional feature support and current-year temporal filtering support |
| Burnable mask | Restricts the negative-pool burnable domain (B4) and supports raster alignment |

All input paths are resolved from the configuration object built by `build_supervised_burned_config()` (`config$inputs`, `config$options`). The config is the single source of truth: there are no hidden path conventions for the run inputs.

## Pool Construction

The supervised stage does not bypass the deterministic stage. It begins by reading `internal_decisions` and auditing the deterministic labels (`audit_deterministic_pools()`, a conservative QA relabelling) before building pools.

- deterministic `keep` polygons become the `burned_pool`,
- deterministic `review` polygons become the `review_pool`,
- the full audited deterministic universe becomes the `scoring_pool`.

The workflow then constructs an `unburned_pool` and merges it with the burned pool to form `train_labeled` (`burned + unburned`).

## Negative Pool

The supervised model uses **two explicit negative sources: random background and Otsu residuals.** There are no other negative buckets.

The negative (unburned) pool follows the historical / canonical method of the supervised Otsu workflow: **burnable-only**. The Otsu residual negative builder runs in `burnable_only` mode, and the random background bucket (B4) is computed **within the burnable domain**. CORINE × ecoregion stratification is used **only** in the deterministic delineation stage (Otsu per CORINE × ecoregion unit); it is **not** used to build the supervised negative pool. Ecoregions are not a feature of the supervised model.

Two builders are combined, in a fixed order so the RNG stream is reproducible:

1. `build_unburned_from_deterministic_decisions()` — provides the **random burnable-background** sample (B4). (The deterministic-drop polygons it reads are *not* training negatives; they remain scoreable but unlabelled.)
2. `build_otsu_negative_pipeline()` — current-year **Otsu residual** patches (drop-only patches, `S_PATCH_PA ≤ 0.15`).

### Random burnable background (B4)

The B4 random-background bucket computes its change-index percentile **and** draws its sample **only within the (aligned) burnable domain**. The burnable mask is applied first; all exclusions and buffers are applied; and only then is the percentile computed over the surviving burnable cells. This is a deliberate methodological correction (Gate 1C.2): earlier code took the percentile over the whole change-index raster, so a run on the current code produces a different — and more correct — negative pool than older runs.

### Content-aware pool fingerprint

Every negative pool is summarised by a deterministic, content-aware fingerprint (`neg_pool_fingerprint`, written as `01_POOLS/<year>_<scenario>_neg_pool_fingerprint.txt`). It folds in the B4 burnable-domain decision, the aligned burnable-mask hash, the percentile configuration and its computed value, the RNG seeds, the exclusions/buffers, and the relevant inputs. Any cache or pool whose fingerprint predates the burnable-domain restriction is **invalidated** rather than silently reused.

### Otsu > random spatial dedup

A location must not enter the negative pool as **both** a random background cell and an Otsu residual patch. After both builders run — and *before* capping and `train_labeled` assembly — every random background row whose polygon intersects any Otsu patch is removed; Otsu rows always have priority and are never touched. The dedup is recorded in `otsu_random_dedup_audit` (`random_before`, `random_removed_by_otsu`, `random_final`, `area_removed`, `removed_ids_hash`) and is folded into the `neg_pool_fingerprint`.

### Unburned pool taxonomy (two sources)

The negative pool routes candidate unburned polygons through **two** independent source buckets, each with its own capacity cap relative to the number of burned training polygons.

| Bucket | Source tag | Cap (× burned) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `random` | random burnable background | 1.0 | Primary, unambiguous negatives (B4, burnable domain) |
| `otsu` | Otsu drop-only patches (`S_PATCH_PA ≤ 0.15`) | 1.0 | Otsu residual patches that were dropped; review/keep excluded |

The two caps are the typed PUBLIC block `negative_pool_params$caps = c(random = 1.0, otsu = 1.0)`, the **single source of truth**; they are mirrored into `cfg$train_control$caps` and forwarded identically to OOF and FINAL. An `Inf` cap disables capping for that bucket.

## Training Eligibility And The Shared Capping Helper

Training eligibility is defined by **explicit class, never by negation**. Every candidate training row is classified by its explicit `class` plus its `(source, neg_type)` metadata:

- `class == "burned"` → **positive** (always kept, never subsampled);
- `class == "unburned"` **and** it resolves to exactly one of the two valid negative buckets above (random, otsu) → **negative**, eligible for capping;
- `class == "unburned"` but a known otsu-excluded type (otsu review / keep patches) → **excluded and logged**, never trained, never an error;
- anything else — `class` `NA` or unknown, or an unburned row with no valid bucket and not a known-excluded type → **hard error** (strict), surfaced with id / class / source / neg_type / origin-stage (OOF or FINAL).

Review / keep / `NA` / unknown / "other" rows can therefore **never** silently become negatives. This replaces the earlier rule that treated negatives as "everything that is not burned" (the OOF `!is_burned` predicate with its `sel_other` / `other_kept` 5th "other" negative category, both removed).

Eligibility resolution and capping live in **two pure internal helpers shared literally by both OOF and FINAL**: an eligibility resolver (`.of_resolve_supervised_eligibility()`, upstream of capping: it assigns buckets, builds the audit table, and logs the excluded ids) and a single canonical capping helper (`.of_cap_negative_buckets()`). The capping helper is the **only** implementation of the cap: `cap = ceiling(n_burned × ratio)`; it takes all available negatives when availability is at or below the cap, keeps every positive, and samples negatives without replacement in a deterministic bucket order, with a per-bucket audit (`bucket, n_burned, n_available, cap_ratio, n_cap_max, n_selected, effective_ratio, seed, context, reason`). The **only** differences between OOF and FINAL are the retained outer-test fold (OOF) and the seed (OOF uses a per-fold fold seed; FINAL uses `cfg$train_control$seeds`). The two stages can no longer diverge on eligibility or capping. This unification is behaviour-preserving for the default 2017 balanced run, where the review/keep/unknown set is empty.

## Spatial Folds And Feature Extraction

After pool construction the workflow builds spatial block folds (`02_FOLDS`), evaluating candidate block sizes and writing a `train_with_folds` layer for spatially structured resampling.

Feature extraction (`03_FEATURES/features_geometry.gpkg`) aligns every support raster to the main annual change-index template before extracting polygon-level summaries from: the main annual change index, post-fire day-of-year support, delayed (autumn-winter) change when available, DEM and slope, grouped CORINE composition, and hotspot density/intensity metrics when hotspot data are available. The mosaic stage remains methodologically central here: every support raster is checked against the same annual template before feature extraction is allowed to proceed.

## Shared Feature Recipe And `_isNA` Indicators

The supervised stage uses ONE feature recipe / builder, shared across the three places a feature space is constructed: the OOF diagnostics, the FINAL refit, and scoring. The recipe defines the **50 base features**, and — critically — **before imputation** it creates a `<feature>_isNA` missing-indicator companion for each base feature (the B5 indicators). The result is **50 base + 50 indicators = 100 columns**, identical across OOF, FINAL and scoring.

This shared recipe is the source of the scoring feature schema: feature names and order, types, the `_isNA` companions, the imputation medians, and the categorical levels all come from the saved FINAL recipe. The scoring matrix is **never** reconstructed from the scoring-year data. The reconciliation policy is recipe-driven and recorded (no silent corrections): a missing feature is created as `NA_real_` (xgboost-missing) plus its `_isNA`; an extra column is dropped; a column-order change is realigned to recipe order; a new categorical level maps to the recipe sentinel.

## Runtime Feature-Schema Parity Guard

A runtime feature-schema parity guard (Gate 1E) enforces the shared-recipe contract on **every run**. It computes a reproducible, wall-clock-free **structural** fingerprint of the feature-space contract — the base-feature names and order, the `_isNA` indicator names and order, `final_feature_order`, the design-matrix column names/order, the `n_base` / `n_indicators` / `n_total` counts, the numeric-vs-factor encoding contract, the feature-weights policy (`_isNA` indicators carry the canonical weight 1.0), and the contract version — while deliberately excluding fit-dependent quantities (imputation medians, learned level values, `scale_pos_weight`, `best_iteration`, seeds, timestamps).

The guard asserts that all OOF outer folds share one canonical contract, that the FINAL refit equals that canonical contract before training/saving, and that the scoring matrix equals the saved FINAL schema before predicting. A structural divergence is an **error** (the run aborts), never a silent warning. The fingerprints and the guard result are written to a `_feature_schema_parity.txt` manifest and returned in the run result.

## Training Procedure

OtsuFire uses a **single** supervised training procedure; there is no protocol choice and no `training_protocol` argument. The number of boosting rounds is selected using an inner validation split and early stopping, and the recipe and model are then refitted on all available training observations before prediction.

Both OOF and the FINAL model go through the same leakage-free core: per-fold/per-final imputation medians and `scale_pos_weight` are fit on training rows only, an inner-validation split is used solely for early stopping, the recipe and model are refit on all training rows at the selected `best_iteration`, and — for OOF — the untouched outer-test fold is then predicted. In the OOF stage the outer-test fold never enters imputation, feature selection, factor levels, weights, round selection or the refit, so the cross-validated diagnostics are leakage-free.

The XGBoost hyperparameters come from `cfg$model_params` and the training controls (caps, seeds, `nrounds_max`, `early_stop`, `val_frac`, imputation rules, `group_col`) from `cfg$train_control` — a single canonical source shared by OOF and FINAL, so the two can never diverge. `scale_pos_weight` is computed per the effective training rows (`n_unburned / n_burned`). OOF always uses the same capped negative-sampling policy as the FINAL model, applied independently within each training fold; there is no `oof_sampling` argument and no "capped vs full" choice. The policy survives only as a fixed, non-settable provenance constant (`cfg$train_control$oof_sampling = "capped"`).

The methodological arguments that still appear on the individual stage functions (`nrounds_max`, `early_stop`, the four `*_to_burned_ratio` caps, `feature_whitelist_override`, `feature_weights`, `val_frac`, `impute_*`, `group_col`, seeds) are **deprecated compatibility shims**: the canonical path is to set them in `build_supervised_burned_config()`. A non-`NULL` override of a canonical default warns (`otsufire_deprecated_param`); an override that conflicts with an explicit builder value errors. They will be removed in a future minor version.

## Internal Validation (OOF)

The one-year workflow writes out-of-fold (OOF) diagnostics to `05_OOF` (aggregate metrics, long-form predictions, labelled OOF summary, recommended thresholds).

What OOF measures and how to read it:

- OOF is an **internal, same-year** diagnostic. Under the nested-refit protocol it holds out an **outer test fold** that is never used for the watchlist, imputation fitting, hyperparameter/threshold selection, or the inner early-stopping split of that fold. The model is fit on the outer-train rows, early-stopped on an **inner validation split**, refit on all outer-train rows at the selected `best_iteration`, and only then predicts the untouched outer-test fold.
- It helps assess model behaviour under spatial autocorrelation (block folds) and supports threshold review.
- **Limit:** the OOF labels are the deterministic-decision labels (the internal `keep`/`drop` audit), not field ground truth. OOF AUC / PR-AUC therefore measure how well the model reproduces the *deterministic decision*, not how well it maps *real fire*. OOF is **not** ground truth, and the supervised stage exports probabilities and diagnostic thresholds rather than forcing a binary burned/unburned classification inside the annual stage.

## External Validation

External validation is a **separate** exercise, performed against an independent reference (EFFIS) with `validate_fire_maps()`. To validate a supervised map, first threshold `p_burned` (or `p_burned_current_year`) into a compatible burned-area prediction layer, then call the shared utility. It reports omission, commission, F1, IoU (plus precision/recall, specificity, balanced accuracy, and area-based coverage metrics).

These external metrics are computed against a **different reference** (EFFIS perimeters) than the OOF metrics (deterministic-decision labels). They are **not comparable** to the OOF AUC / PR-AUC: a model can reproduce the deterministic decision well (high OOF AUC) and still omit or over-detect against EFFIS, or vice versa. Keep the two evaluations distinct.

## Scores: `p_burned` Is A Model Score

`p_burned` (and the temporally adjusted `p_burned_current_year`) is a **model score under the training distribution** produced by `binary:logistic`. It is on the (0, 1) scale but it must **not** be described as a calibrated probability without an explicit calibration step (e.g. Platt/isotonic against a held-out reference), which the pipeline does not currently perform. Treat the score as a ranking / relative-confidence signal and select an operating threshold from the OOF diagnostics or external validation.

## Final Model, Public Map, And Outputs

After OOF, the runtime trains the FINAL model (`07_FINAL_MODEL_V2`), scores the full deterministic universe (`08_SCORED`), and writes the annual supervised maps (`09_FINAL_MAP`).

| Output | Current role |
|---|---|
| `final_map_full` | Complete scored deterministic universe (auditability) |
| `final_map` | Current-year public map after temporal adjustment and column selection |
| `burned_like_scored` | Scored burned-like subset (exported when `export_burned_like = TRUE`) |

The final scorer applies a current-year temporal adjustment before producing the public map, combining previous-year overlap and hotspot-density support to compute `p_burned_model`, `temporal_penalty`, `p_burned_current_year`, and `temporal_conflict_flag`. The public `final_map` is derived from that adjusted annual view; `final_map_full` preserves the complete scored universe.

## Post-Threshold Validation

To validate a supervised map externally, threshold `p_burned` / `p_burned_current_year` into a burned-area prediction layer and call `validate_fire_maps()` against the EFFIS reference (see **External Validation** above). This keeps validation workflow-independent and does not turn the supervised stage into a forced binary classifier.

`check_supervised_consistency()` separately compares the deterministic and supervised outputs of the same run and writes per-issue diagnostic artefacts; it is invoked automatically when `run_oneyear_supervised_pipeline(..., run_consistency = TRUE)`.

## Removed: Supervised Burned-Like Registry (Closed Branch)

Earlier designs of this stage maintained a scenario-specific *supervised burned-like registry* (`burned_high_conf_registry_candidates` / `burned_high_conf_registry` under `Results/<SCENARIO_UPPER>/`) and an associated positive-pool augmentation path (Mode B / `historical_registry_augment`). Both are **removed from the current package**:

- The Mode B registry-based positive-pool augmentation was formally rejected on 2026-04-17 (a closed rejected branch, not a pending feature).
- The supervised registry *products* and the `append_supervised_registry()` step were removed from the runtime on 2026-06-05 (§N+27). The supervised pipeline no longer writes a scenario registry.

The scored burned-like subset is still available as the ordinary `burned_like_scored` output, but it is no longer routed into any registry. This is distinct from the deterministic stage's RBR keep-pool / keep-reference registry (`collect_keep_reference_samples()`, `build_keep_pool_from_samples()`, `RBR_TRAINING_REGISTRY.gpkg`), which is a separate, still-supported deterministic feature.

## Corrected Defect: OOF / FINAL `_isNA` Divergence (Gate 1D.8)

A defect was found and corrected during Gate 1D.8, before the smoke run and before the definitive run:

- Previously, **OOF generated the `_isNA` missing-indicator companions, but the FINAL refit and scoring did NOT use them**. OOF therefore evaluated a model trained on a 102-column feature space (51 base + 51 indicators) while the deployed FINAL model and scoring ran on a different (51-column) space.
- Consequently, the **prior OOF diagnostics did not exactly represent the deployed model**: they characterised a different feature space than the one actually scored.
- The **prior FINAL was not necessarily invalid**, but it was a **different model** than the one OOF evaluated.
- The correction unified all three paths (OOF, FINAL, scoring) on the **same recipe** and was made **before the smoke and before the definitive 2017 run**.
- **Definitive results require RETRAINING both models** (OOF and FINAL) under the corrected common recipe; results carried over from before the fix do not apply.

Any baseline produced under the current code uses the single canonical training procedure (inner-early-stopping selection + full-data refit) over the corrected common feature recipe. It is **not** an exact reproduction of the old 51-feature FINAL model, because the feature recipe (and therefore the feature space) changed when the `_isNA` indicators were unified across the three paths.

## LOYO And Historical Application: Current Documented Status

::: {.callout-warning}
The current sources do not yet support a full operational tutorial for LOYO or historical application.

- LOYO is a separate temporal-validation concept; the replacement multiyear runtime is still pending.
- Historical application is supported conceptually by the paper draft but lacks a stable, current step-by-step entry point in the package.
:::

For now, the safe interpretation is:

- one-year supervised plus OOF is the documented operational annual workflow,
- LOYO is a separate validation concept still pending redesign,
- historical transfer is a concept in the paper draft but is not backed by a current package runtime (the former supervised registry that would have supported it has been removed).
